Chapter 6: The Everyday Practice of Enough.
You know, most of us wake up in the morning not feeling all that different from the day before. Those old doubts—they still linger, don’t they? Just waiting for a quiet moment to sneak back in. But here’s where the real magic happens—it’s not in some huge, overnight transformation. It’s in those tiny, everyday choices. The ones you make, again and again, to live from a place of enough.
Imagine a woman who starts each day with a simple ritual. Before she checks her phone, before she dives into that endless to-do list, she just sits. Quietly. She breathes in the silence and gently reminds herself, “My value isn’t tied to what I accomplish today.” Sometimes, those words feel a little empty. But she says them anyway. And slowly, this practice becomes her anchor—a gentle way to steady herself before the world comes rushing in.
Then there’s someone else, gearing up for a tough meeting at work. She feels that old anxiety creeping up—the urge to prove herself, to stand out, to be the best in the room. But she pauses. She remembers: her worth isn’t on the line. So she walks in with just a bit more ease, a little less hungry for approval. The meeting? It’s not perfect. But she leaves with her confidence still intact.
A lot of us think confidence is a destination—like, one day you’ll arrive and never have to worry about it again. But really, it’s more like a muscle. The more you use it, the stronger it gets. Every time you choose to believe you’re enough—even when doubt is whispering in your ear—that muscle grows just a little.
These practices aren’t flashy. They show up in how you talk to yourself after a mistake, in your choice to rest instead of constantly pushing, and in the courage it takes to say no when you need boundaries.
Of course, there are setbacks. Old habits can creep back in, and those lies can sound awfully convincing. But here’s the difference—now, you notice them. You can call out those old stories, challenge them, even replace them with something kinder. The more you practice, the easier it gets. And that voice—the one that quietly says you’re enough? It grows clearer, a little stronger, with every single day.
